_note: English source for the landing page. Every other file in this folder has exactly these keys. Keys ending in _html may contain the {email} placeholder, nothing else. hero_bubble breaks onto its second line at \n. Brand names stay as they are: Grasp, App Store, iPhone, Android.
title: Grasp — your workout planned, your weights worked out
description: Grasp plans your workout and works out your weights from what you lifted last time. Free on Android and iPhone, no ads, works offline.
og_description: Plans your workout and works out your weights from last time. Free, no ads, works offline.
hero_lede: Tell it your goal and the equipment you have, and it plans your workout. Your weights come from what you lifted last time.
store_aria: Download Grasp on the App Store
hero_meta: Free on Android and iPhone, in 15 languages. No subscription, nothing to unlock.
lang_lede: Not just the menus: every screen, every exercise name and its step-by-step instructions.
plan_title: Your next workout, built for you
plan_body: Tell it your goal, how many days you train, how long a session is and what equipment you can actually reach. It will never suggest a movement you cannot do. Save a setup for every place you train, and switching gyms rebuilds today's session.
plan_alt: Grasp's workout screen: eight exercises planned for a full-body muscle-building session, each with its weight
equip_title: Tick what you have. It plans with nothing else.
equip_body: A few dumbbells at home, a full rack at the gym, a band in a hotel room: save a setup for each place and switch in one tap. Grasp only plans exercises you can do with what is ticked, and rebuilds today's session when you switch.
equip_note_home: Home: 5 of 58 pieces ticked, so every exercise is one you can do there.
equip_note_gym: Gym: everything ticked, so the whole library is open.
equip_note_tail: Over 50 kinds of equipment to choose from.
routine_title: Your own routines, set by set
routine_body1: Prefer your own program? Build a routine and set every set the way you want it: warm-up, normal, drop set or to failure, an exact number of reps or a range, and your own rest. Grasp still fills in the weights from your last session, and you can change any number.
routine_body2: Pair exercises into supersets and drag them into order. Switch between the Grasp plan and your routines in one tap, and when a workout goes differently, choose whether the routine changes with it.
routine_alt: A routine in Grasp: Barbell Bench Press set by set, a warm-up, two working sets and a drop set, then a superset of Cable Fly and Dumbbell Lateral Raise
prog_title: Your weights go up with you
prog_body1: Hit the top of your rep range on every set and the weight goes up. Don't like it? Change it in one tap.
prog_ledger_why: Every set reached the top of your range — up 5 kg.
prog_body2: Miss it twice and it comes down. Five kilograms here because that is the smallest step on the machine. Warm-up sets are worked out from your working weight, and the rest timer starts itself.
prog_alt: An exercise in Grasp: an animation of the movement, warm-up sets, and last time's weight
pr_body1: Lift your heaviest weight, beat your best estimated max, do your biggest set or more reps than ever, and Grasp marks it the moment you log the set.
pr_body2: The workout summary lists every record you set. Records are worked out from the sets you logged, so fixing a mistyped set fixes the record too.
pr_alt: New personal records in Grasp: 85 kg for 6 on the Barbell Bench Press and 12 reps on the Pull-Up, each marked with a trophy, and a summary of the four records
pr_banner_note: Heaviest weight: 85 kg, up from 82.5 kg
recap_body: On the 1st of every month, last month arrives as a few cards: the days you trained, the hours, the weight you lifted, your biggest jump and what you trained most, next to the month before. Grasp has something to say on every card, and there is a year in review too.
share_body: Finish a workout and share it as a card made for stories. Break a record and Grasp is on the card holding the trophy. You can also send a routine as a link, and your friend opens it straight in Grasp.
rec_body: A body map shades each muscle by how recently you worked it, so a week of training reads at a glance instead of needing to be added up. Muscles fade as they recover.
rec_alt: Grasp's body map, with the muscles trained today highlighted
vol_body: Sets are counted against a weekly target for each muscle group, and you can change the target. You can see where the week's effort went, and what is still short.
vol_alt: Grasp's weekly targets: sets done per muscle group against a target
int_body: Rope, sprints, planks: work and rest, counted for you, with a sound at every change so you can put the phone down. Save your own presets. Between sets, the rest timer rings and counts down in the notification shade.
int_alt: Grasp's interval timer with work, rest and round settings
log_body: Everything lives on your phone and works with no signal. An account only backs your training up so it survives a lost phone. Export everything as a spreadsheet or a complete backup whenever you want. It is your training, in a format you can open.
log_alt: Grasp's training log on a calendar
ai_p1: No AI decides what you lift. It is plain maths you can check: set targets per muscle, what you logged, and one simple rule for the weights.
ai_p2: That is also why it works on your phone with no signal.
final_lede: Free on Android and iPhone. No ads, no subscription, nothing to unlock.
final_meta_html: Questions? Email {email}. Gyms and brands interested in working together, same address.
disclaimer: Grasp suggests training weights from what you log. It is not medical advice and it cannot see your form or your health. Talk to a doctor before starting a new training program, particularly if you have an injury or a health condition.
faq1_a: Yes. Grasp is completely free: no ads, no subscription, no paid tier and nothing to unlock.
faq2_a: Yes. Your workout and your weights are worked out on your phone, so it works in a gym with no signal. Only the first sign-up needs internet. The account is there to back up your training.
faq3_a: 15: English, Arabic, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Turkish, Polish, Russian, Hindi, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Indonesian and Portuguese. That includes the exercise names and the step-by-step instructions.
faq4_q: Can I train at home with just dumbbells?
faq4_a: Yes. Tick the equipment you have and Grasp only plans exercises you can do with it. Save a setup for home, the gym or a hotel and switch in one tap.
faq5_q: Can I make my own routines?
faq5_a: Yes. Build as many routines as you like, set by set: warm-ups, drop sets, sets to failure, exact reps or a range, and supersets. Grasp fills in the weights from your last session, and you can switch back to the Grasp plan any day.
faq6_q: How does Grasp pick my weights?
faq6_a: From what you logged last time. Reach the top of your rep range on every set and the weight goes up. Miss it twice and it comes down. You can change any weight in one tap.
faq7_a: No. It uses simple rules that run on your phone, which is why it works offline.
faq8_a: Yes. Grasp is free on Google Play for Android and on the App Store for iPhone.
faq9_a: Not for advertising. Grasp records which screens and features you use, never your weights or health data, to make the app better, and you can switch that off under Account. It does not use advertising identifiers, and it does not ask for your location, contacts or microphone. The camera only opens when you take a photo for a share card.
